guide.title: Cold Exposure & Hypothermia
guide.lead: Handle the cold patient like glass: rough movement can trigger VF. Stage by consciousness and shivering, insulate and warm the trunk, take up to a minute to find a pulse, and remember that a cold heart can recover after very long CPR.

sections.title: Stage it (Swiss staging)
notes: No thermometer? Stage by consciousness and shivering.

steps.title: Gentle
steps.text: Keep horizontal; avoid rough handling and jolts.

steps.title: Stop heat loss
steps.text: Remove wet clothing (cut it), insulate top and bottom, vapour barrier, cover the head.

figures.alt: A "hypothermia wrap": insulating mat underneath, vapour barrier, sleeping bag, outer shell, head covered, heat packs on the chest and armpits.

steps.title: Warm the trunk
steps.text: Heat packs or blankets to chest, armpits and back; warm IV fluids (38–42 °C) per protocol. Mild and shivering: warm sweet drinks if able to swallow.

steps.title: Destination
steps.text: Severe or unstable: a centre with ECLS (bypass) if possible.

steps.title: Check for life
steps.text: Breathing and pulse for up to 1 minute: severe bradycardia can feel like no pulse.

steps.title: CPR
steps.text: Standard rate and depth; mechanical CPR helps long transports. Rigid chest is expected.

steps.title: Shocks
steps.text: Below 30 °C: up to 3 shocks; if VF persists, hold further shocks until above 30 °C (ERC). AHA allows standard defibrillation alongside rewarming.

steps.title: Drugs
steps.text: Below 30 °C: withhold epinephrine. 30–35 °C: double the interval (every 6–10 minutes) (ERC).

steps.title: Don't stop early
steps.text: Not dead until warm and dead – unless injuries incompatible with life, a frozen chest, or an avalanche burial over 60 minutes with a blocked airway.

sections.title: Local cold injuries
rows: Pale, numb, soft; recovers with warming
White or grey, hard, waxy; blisters after thawing
Treat hypothermia first. Thaw only if it won't refreeze: water at 37–39 °C for 15–30 minutes. No rubbing, no dry heat. Ibuprofen, pad and protect blisters
Cold, wet, numb for days, then red and painful
Dry gently, warm, elevate; don't rub

items.label: Bradycardia
items.sub: Expected in moderate and severe hypothermia; pacing rarely needed.

items.label: Atrial fibrillation
items.sub: Common below 32 °C; usually settles with rewarming.

items.label: VF
items.sub: Rough handling can trigger it; up to 3 shocks below 30 °C.

quiz.q: Found outside on a freezing night: unresponsive, not shivering, pupils dilated. After a long check you feel a slow carotid pulse. You:
options: Don't start CPR: handle gently, insulate, warm the trunk, transport
quiz.explanation: Compressions on a perfusing heart can trigger VF.

quiz.q: Core 25.6 °C, pulseless; VF persists after 3 shocks. Per ERC you:
options: Hold further shocks until above 30 °C and continue CPR with rewarming
quiz.explanation: AHA allows standard shocks alongside rewarming.

quiz.q: Moderate hypothermia with frozen hands. Priority?
options: Rewarm the core first; protect the hands
Warm hands and core together in hot water
quiz.explanation: Hypothermia kills; frostbite doesn't in the short term.

options: Check for a pulse for up to 1 minute; prolonged CPR with rewarming can succeed
Give standard drugs at any temperature
quiz.explanation: Not dead until warm and dead.

quiz.q: A patient who is drowsy and has stopped shivering is in which stage?
Why handle a hypothermic patient gently?
options: The cold heart is irritable and VF can be triggered

quiz.q: Frostbite should be thawed in water at:
Best destination for a hypothermic arrest:

options: Gentle handling and warming the trunk, not the limbs
quiz.explanation: Cold blood from the limbs returns to the core.

flashcards.question: Hypothermia stages
flashcards.answer: Mild 32–35 °C (alert, shivering); moderate 28–32 °C (drowsy, shivering stops); severe below 28 °C (unconscious); arrest often below 24 °C.

flashcards.question: Gentle handling
flashcards.answer: The cold heart is irritable: jolts, rough moves and aggressive suction can trigger VF. Keep the patient horizontal.

flashcards.question: Afterdrop
flashcards.answer: Core temperature keeps falling after rescue as cold blood returns from the limbs. Handle gently and warm the trunk first.

flashcards.question: Frostbite care
flashcards.answer: No rubbing, no dry heat. Thaw only if it won't refreeze: 37–39 °C water for 15–30 minutes. Ibuprofen, pain relief, protect blisters.

flashcards.question: Shocks and drugs below 30 °C
flashcards.answer: ERC: up to 3 shocks, then wait until above 30 °C; withhold epinephrine below 30 °C, double the interval at 30–35 °C. AHA: standard shocks with rewarming.

flashcards.question: Pulse check in hypothermia
flashcards.answer: Up to 1 minute for breathing and pulse: profound bradycardia is easy to miss.

flashcards.question: Rewarming
flashcards.answer: Insulate and stop heat loss; heat packs to the trunk; warm IV fluids; warm drinks only if alert and swallowing. Arrest or unstable: ECLS centre.

flashcards.question: Trench (immersion) foot
flashcards.answer: Non-freezing injury from days of cold, wet feet: numb and pale, then red and painful. Dry, warm gently, elevate, don't rub.

critical.scenario: Lost hiker found after 4 hours in sub-zero wind: unresponsive, not shivering, rigid. After 20 seconds you can't feel a pulse.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Keep checking breathing and pulse for up to 1 minute (monitor too); if none, start CPR, handle gently, insulate and head for an ECLS centre

options.f: Profound bradycardia needs a longer check.
Not dead until warm and dead.

options.t: Rub his limbs to warm him

critical.explanation: Mechanical CPR makes long transports possible.
critical.kpi: Performs prolonged pulse check and appropriate hypothermic resuscitation

critical.scenario: 68-year-old in an unheated flat during a power cut: confused, shivering, cold pale skin, can swallow.
critical.question: Stage and rewarming?

options.t: Mild hypothermia: remove wet clothes, insulate, warm room or ambulance, warm sweet drinks, heat to the trunk, transport

critical.explanation: Shivering is the body's best heater: support it with calories.
critical.kpi: Stages hypothermia and selects passive and active external rewarming

critical.scenario: 52-year-old slept outside in freezing weather: confused, hands white and hard, feet frozen. He walked to the shelter on them; your transport is 2 hours with no reliable heating.
critical.question: Correct management?

options.t: Treat hypothermia first; don't thaw the hands and feet if they may refreeze – protect, pad and splint them, ibuprofen, transport
Have him walk to the ambulance
options.f: He's already walked on them; carry him now.

critical.explanation: Thaw once in a controlled setting, ideally with specialist care.
critical.kpi: Manages frostbite with refreeze risk correctly
